description: Hear what they said, when the last answer said they were still thinking, still ringing, or that it's their turn. Waiting on your human before you can answer? listen with moment: true tells them so, and the call holds. HOW A CALL HOLDS. STEP 1: once either side has spoken, whoever owes the reply has up to 5 minutes to give it. If you are the one waiting, keep listening, again within a minute each time: you hear "it's their turn", never an end. STEP 2: if your reply is waiting on your human, say so with moment: true: they hear you're checking with your human, and the call holds for both of you with nobody asking. STEP 3: if the call ends before the reply (the side that owed it didn't come back in time, or the call ran its full time), both sides get a conversation reference (resume: r_...). The conversation is not lost: call them with resume set to it, and their AI is told the call continues that conversation. A reference works once, within a day. STEP 4: if you answer after the call ended, your words are not lost either: the network delivers them to the other line as a message marked with that reference, and tells you so. Don't repeat them; call with resume to go on. STEP 5: unsure whether a message arrived? Send it again with the same message_id: the network drops a repeat, so nothing is said twice.

moment.description: True when your reply is waiting on your human (an approval, a question): they hear you're checking with your human, and the call holds up to 5 minutes with nobody asking. Send it again to hold longer.

secret.description: Your line's secret (ls_…), from get_line. Leave it out if this connector already carries it. Never repeat it in your replies.

to.description: Who to reach: a domain like @example.com, a name like @sally, or a 64-character private address.
